fixed.what: realProc's three PowerShell texts now start with $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' (shared PS_PREFIX), so a failed CIM query exits non-zero: alive and boot return null and list throws proc-unavailable 2. alive() maps its output through the new exported pure function aliveFromQuery: only 'NONE' means dead, and any output that is not NONE, NOSTART or an ISO time is null (unknown). The texts are exported read-only as PS_SCRIPTS.
fixed.test_added: T36m (pure: every PS_SCRIPTS text starts with the Stop preference); T89b (one real PowerShell per text, with Get-CimInstance shadowed by a function that writes a non-terminating error: the alive and list texts must exit non-zero and never print NONE). Against the unfixed text T89b failed with 'alive: exited 0 with stdout NONE', which is the reviewer's reproduction.

fixed.what: realProc.alive compares one-sidedly via aliveFromQuery: the listed process is the holder iff its CreationDate <= the recorded start + START_TOLERANCE_MS. A slow start-up no longer reads as dead; a pid reused by a later process is still told apart. sameStartTime itself is unchanged, because other scripts use it.
fixed.test_added: T36l (aliveFromQuery cases: 12 s of start-up is alive, a process created 2.5 s after the recorded start is pid reuse, junk output is null). It fails against the symmetric compare. T85's existing assertions still pass.

fixed.what: acquireLock judges a holder only after its lock bytes have stayed unchanged for min(LOCK_JUDGE_AFTER=50, retries) consecutive sightings. This is a retry counter with no clock read, so ordinary contention starts no PowerShell; a caller with fewer retries still judges at its last retry. breakStale re-reads the lock right before the rename and skips the break ('changed') when the bytes differ from the ones judged. readLockRecord now also returns the raw bytes.
fixed.test_added: T36g (with retries 60, alive is called once, at sighting 51); T36h (a lock whose bytes change on every read is never judged and the call ends lock-busy 75); T36i (a lock replaced between the judgement and the break is never renamed). All three fail against the old loop.

fixed.what: An unreadable lock file (empty or not a record) that stays byte-for-byte unchanged for the whole retry budget is broken when retries >= LOCK_UNREADABLE_MIN_RETRIES (50; scripts pass 300, about 30 s). The break uses the same protocol as a stale break: pre-rename re-read, rename, compare bytes, create with wx, else restore by link. No process query is made. The lock-break line keeps the contract shape stale {pid,start_time,nonce,script}, all null, and adds data.unreadable {bytes, sha256}. With fewer retries the lock stays, as before (lock-busy 75).
fixed.test_added: T36j (empty and truncated-JSON locks stay with retries 3; with retries 50 they are broken, with no process query and a correct lock-break line); T36k (guard: an unreadable lock that becomes a live record during the budget is not broken). T36j fails against the old code.

fixed.what: No library change was needed: the assertHeld guards at appendLedger (before writeLedgerLine) and writeTasks (before writeAtomic) were already present but untested.
fixed.test_added: T42b (the run.lock nonce is swapped when tailInfo opens ledger.jsonl: lock-lost 75 and the ledger bytes are unchanged); T50b (the nonce is swapped when writeTasks reads tasks.json: lock-lost 75, and tasks.json and .prev are unchanged). Both fail when the respective assertHeld is replaced by void 0 (M11 and its writeTasks twin).

fixed.what: T21 now wraps the 200 writes in try/finally. The finally always writes the stop file, waits up to 10 s for the reader (the timer is cleared), and kills the reader only if it is still running. No child is left when writeAtomic throws.
fixed.test_added: None separate, because the fix is to the test itself; T21 still passes (2.6 s).

fixed.what: Fixed in lib with no schema or file-format change; card.schema.json is untouched. wordCount now also splits on Unicode format characters (category Cf, e.g. U+200B and U+2060) and counts every Han, Hiragana or Katakana character as one word. The x-maxWords check also refuses any string longer than x-maxWords * MAX_CODEPOINTS_PER_WORD (40) code points, reported under keyword x-maxWords.
fixed.test_added: T67b: 500 tokens joined by U+200B or by U+2060 are refused, and so are 16 Han or 16 Hiragana characters and a token of 601 code points; 15 Han characters and a 600-code-point token pass, and ordinary counts are unchanged. T67b fails against the old wordCount. T67 still passes.

not_fixed.why: The suggestion to report a lock-unreadable anomaly belongs in status.mjs, which is not my file. The library now breaks such a lock after a full retry budget, so it no longer blocks forever. A status anomaly would still help while the lock is waiting.

A backward wall-clock step of more than 2 s between the holder's creation and its own start-time reading still makes a live holder look like a later process. The one-sided rule cannot tell this from pid reuse without a different lock record format, and format changes are out of scope.

tests.command: node tools/lane.mjs --label lib-fix --timeout-s 300 -- node --test --test-concurrency=1 tcb/test/lib.test.mjs (cwd tcb-build)
tests.output_tail: Full suite: 190 tests, 188 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 2 skipped (T82, T92 need the app), 79958 ms. Mutation check (lane label lib-fix-mut): all eight fixes were reverted together in place, after a backup at tmp/lib.mjs.fixed. The reverted changes were the assertHeld in appendLedger and in writeTasks, the Stop preference, the one-sided compare, the judge-after count, the pre-rename re-read, the unreadable break, and the wordCount change with its length cap. Against that, all 10 targeted tests failed: T36g, T36h, T36i, T36j, T36l, T36m, T42b, T50b, T67b and T89b. The guard test T36k passed both times, as intended. lib.mjs was then restored and checked byte-identical to the fixed copy. Return file: done/lib-fix.json, checked as valid JSON through the lane. One lapse: a single trivial `node -e` JSON check ran outside the lane once; it was then repeated inside the lane.

lib_change_requests: Other files (not mine): status.mjs:129 and :627 and handover.mjs:131 judge lock holders with lib.sameStartTime, which is symmetric. They should use the one-sided rule of lib.aliveFromQuery (listed start <= recorded + tolerance) for the same reason as LR-2.
Other files (not mine): status.mjs should report an unreadable run.lock or watcher.lock as an anomaly (LR-4).

Other files (not mine): commit.mjs:370 uses lib.wordCount for index summaries. It now also splits on Unicode format characters and counts CJK characters as words, so rerun the commit tests. Every schema field with x-maxWords now also has a length bound of 40 code points per word: rerun the tests of the scripts that validate cards, fmea, hazards, review, sentence and stpa.
